title: coax tells decade how to start it again with a restore block
body:
decade restarts coax on restore through a path of its own. coax's hello carries an `agent` block (`decade_channel::Agent`, built in `run` in `src/app.rs`) with the session id and `resume_args`. decade saves those and, on restore, types `coax <args> --session <id>` into a ghostty.

decade now gives every decade-aware program a general way to say how it starts again: a restore block, sent with `Channel::restore(&Restore)` from `decade-channel` (`Restore { argv, terminal }`). decade is dropping its coax special case (decade issue decade-a14cb8) and will restart coax only through that block.

## Proposal

- Right after `Channel::connect` in `report::connect`, coax sends a restore block whose argv is `coax`, then `agent.args`, then `--session <id>`, with `terminal` true.
- When the session coax runs on changes while it runs, coax sends the block again with the new id.
- The `agent` block stays as it is. decade still uses its session id to attach a returning agent to its card.

## Cost

coax must ship this before or with the decade build that drops the special case. A running coax without it is not restarted by that decade. `decade-channel` is a path dependency, so the new call is already there.
